previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, consistent with her history of type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and chronic pancreatitis. She presented with hyperglycemia and an elevated anion gap of 23, indicating diabetic ketoacidosis. She initially refused insulin but later accepted an insulin drip, which helped close the anion gap. She declined potassium repletion and additional testing. Despite clinical improvement, she requested to leave against medical advice due to discomfort with the hospital environment and a desire to manage her care at home. She demonstrated the ability to self-administer insulin and was given 15 units of long-acting insulin upon discharge. She was discharged home with instructions to continue her insulin regimen and monitor for worsening symptoms.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with IDDM, chronic pancreatitis and gastroparesis presents 
with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain in the setting of 
insulin noncompliance for several days. 
. 
#. Nausea, Vomiting, Abdominal Pain: 
Admission ddx included diabetic gastroparesis, pancreatitis 
flare, and/or complications of hyperglycemia. We note that she 
had elevated lactate and hyponatremia on admission which may 
also have contributed. Symptoms resolved within 24 hours of 
admission with normalization of her blood sugars, IVF, and home 
PRN compazine. She tolerated a full regular (diabetic) diet for 
48h prior to discharge. She did have recurrent symptoms (milder) 
on the day of discharge in the setting of having restarted tube 
feeds for 24h. This also resolved w/home meds + 1 dose IV zofran 
+ IV acetominophen.
.
#. Diabetes
Blood sugar control was problematic during this admission. 
During the first ___, while holding tube feeds, she had two 
episodes of symptomatic mid-morning hypoglycemia. BS ranged high 
(>500) after tube feeds restarted. ___ consult followed 
carefully and modified her insulin regimen as-needed by 
decreasing insulin sliding scales and ___ lantus. She was 
normoglycemic for >12h before discharge. Discharged with plan 
for close follow-up by PCP and ___ transitional 
clinic, including ongoing discussion of whether tubefeeds might 
be stopped in the setting of excellent PO intake witnessed in 
the hospital.
. 
#. Hyponatremia on admission 
We note that admission serum sodium was 126, which corrects to 
136 in setting of serum glucose of 744. Serum corrected to wnl 
on labs as hyperglycemia resolved.
. 
#. Reported hx recent pneumonia  
Patient reported history of a recent pneumonia diagnosed at 
___, although history and the treatment she 
describes sounds more like an asthma/COPD flare. No focal 
findings on physical exam. No SOB or hypoxia. CXR clear. She was 
continued on her home inhalers; did not receive any steroids or 
antibiotics.
.
